name: Laxmi Misthan Bhandar (LMB)
why_it_matters: A 300-year-old Marwari sweet shop and pure-veg restaurant in the heart of Johari Bazaar, claimed to be Rajasthan's first three-star hotel. The pyaaz kachori and ghevar are the dishes Jaipur sends to relatives in Bombay.
insider_tip: Skip the ground-floor sweet counter queue and head upstairs to the dining hall — the seated thali experience is faster than the takeaway crush during festivals.
signature_address: 98-99, Johari Bazaar Road, Bapu Bazaar, Biseswarji, Jaipur 302003

name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
why_it_matters: The Rawat family claims to have invented Jaipur's pyaaz kachori at this Station Road shop. Onion, garlic and red chilli for the filling come from their own farm near Jodhpur, and groundnut oil is shipped from Gujarat — a closed supply chain that explains the consistency.
insider_tip: The 7-9am window is when the kachoris are freshest; by afternoon the morning batch has been re-fried. Order kadhi kachori — they slit the kachori and ladle hot kadhi inside.
signature_address: Polo Victory Cinema, Sindhi Camp, Station Road, Jaipur 302006

name: Sahu ki Chai
why_it_matters: Opened by Late Shree Ladhu Ram ji in 1968, this footpath stall on Chaura Rasta runs 365 days a year. Milk is slow-simmered over coal in weathered pots — the long reduction is what local foodies say sets it apart from MI Road chai stops.
insider_tip: Park outside Sai Baba Temple and walk in — Chaura Rasta is a one-way mess for cars. Grab the first kulhad you're handed; they're served at the speed of arrival, not order.
signature_address: Shop No. 365, Opposite Sai Baba Temple, Chaura Rasta, Jaipur 302003

name: Gulab Ji Chai Wale
why_it_matters: Started by Gulab Singh Dheerawat as a tea cart in 1947, now run from a hole-in-the-wall opposite Ganpati Plaza on MI Road. Roughly 100kg of tea-grade milk goes through the kettles between 4:30am and 8pm — the bun-samosa here is the dish locals queue past politicians for.
insider_tip: Order bun maska samosa, not just chai — the slit-bun stuffed with samosa filling is the one Jaipur regulars come for. Cash only.
signature_address: Opposite Ganpati Plaza, MI Road, Jaipur 302001

name: Bombay Misthan Bhandar (BMB)
why_it_matters: BMB has been the Old City's parallel sweet institution to LMB since the 1950s — desi-ghee sweets, Sawan-season ghevar, and a kachori counter that runs from 6:30am. Multiple branches, but the Johari Bazaar one is the original.
insider_tip: Ghevar is a Teej-Rakhi monsoon sweet — visit between July and September for the freshest stock. The malai ghevar comes assembled-to-order so it doesn't go soggy.
signature_address: Near Sanganeri Gate, Johari Bazaar, Jaipur 302003

name: Kanji Sweets
why_it_matters: Naya Bazaar standalone shop that locals route the Jaipur 'kachori trail' to as the final stop. Big-bowl Raj Kachori with sev, dahi, tamarind chutney and pomegranate — and a kullad of malai-topped lassi to chase it.
insider_tip: The malai lassi is in unmarked terracotta kullads behind the counter — point and ask. It's served cold by 11am; afternoon batches lose the chill.
signature_address: Naya Bazaar, near Chandpole Gate, Jaipur 302002

name: Masala Chowk
why_it_matters: Open-air food court inside Ramniwas Bagh, opposite Albert Hall, opened 26 January 2018 by JDA to consolidate 20+ Pink City street-food vendors in one cleaner space. Single ticket entry, then pay per stall.
insider_tip: Entry is ₹13. Skip lunchtime — go between 4-7pm when the chaat stalls have just done their afternoon prep and the Albert Hall lights come on next door for free post-meal viewing.
signature_address: Ramniwas Bagh, near Albert Hall Museum, Jaipur 302004
